query: best mattresses for side sleepers in 2026
description: The Helix Midnight Luxe tops our 7 mattresses for side sleepers: a medium hybrid with zoned coils. Picks by body weight and by hip, shoulder and back pain.
dek: The Helix Midnight Luxe is the best mattress for side sleepers for most: a medium hybrid with zoned support.
intro: A medium-feel hybrid with a thick pressure-relieving comfort layer over zoned coils wins for most side sleepers, because it lets the shoulder and hip sink in while firmer support holds the waist up and keeps the spine level. Here are the seven worth a look, matched to body weight, hip pain and back pain.

Side sleeping puts your whole body weight on two narrow points, the shoulder and the hip. A mattress that is too firm pushes back hard on both, and one that is too soft lets the hips sag. The right bed sits in between, and where exactly depends mostly on how much you weigh.
quickAnswer: the Helix Midnight Luxe Mattress is our #1 pick (best overall). The Helix Midnight Luxe is the best mattress for most side sleepers because it pairs a deep, pressure-relieving pillow top with zoned coils that keep the lower back supported.

sections.h: The 7 Best Mattresses for Side Sleepers in 2026, Ranked

blocks.p: We did not sleep on or test these mattresses. The picks come from manufacturer specifications, materials and layer construction, trial and warranty terms, and recurring owner feedback, weighed against what a side sleeper actually needs: enough cushioning for the shoulder and hip, and enough support under the waist. Where makers and retail listings disagree on a figure, such as trial length or firmness, we say so in the write-up rather than pick the flattering number. Firmness is given as the maker states it unless noted.

On top is a gel memory foam pillow top quilted into the cover, followed by a thick high-density memory foam comfort layer and a transition foam. Underneath sits a layer of individually wrapped coils that Helix says are zoned: firmer-gauge coils under the lower back and softer coils under the shoulders. That is precisely the shape of support a side sleeper wants, with the shoulder free to sink while the waist stays up. Helix calls the feel medium, and reviewers broadly agree, with Sleepopolis scoring it around 6.5 on its own 10-point scale. Reviewers rate it well for side sleepers across light, average and heavy weights, though some suggest sleepers over roughly 230 to 250 pounds may want something firmer. sections.h: What Is the Best Mattress for Side Sleepers?

blocks.p: For most side sleepers, buy the Helix Midnight Luxe. Helix calls it a medium hybrid built for side sleepers, with a gel memory foam pillow top over zoned coils that are firmer under the lower back. That is exactly the brief: soft at the shoulder, supportive at the waist.

If your shoulder is the main complaint, the Purple Restore Hybrid (Soft) uses a grid that buckles under pressure points. The TEMPUR-Cloud is the memory foam pick. Over about 230 pounds, look at the Brooklyn Bedding Signature Hybrid. The Leesa Original Hybrid suits combination sleepers, the Nectar Classic is the value foam bed, and the Zinus Green Tea is the budget choice.

Body weight decides firmness, and firmness decides everything else. A 120-pound side sleeper on a medium-firm bed barely sinks, so the shoulder takes the load. A 260-pound side sleeper on a soft bed sinks too far at the hips. Match the feel to your weight first, then choose foam or coils.
Shopping for other sleep positions too? Our [guide to the top rated mattresses](/best-mattress/) covers back and stomach sleepers. This page stays on side sleeping, including hip pain and back pain.

sections.h: How Do the 7 Side Sleeper Mattresses Compare?

blocks.p: Height and feel below are as the maker or listing states them. Trial and warranty terms on Amazon can differ from a direct purchase, so confirm them on the listing.

Four of the seven are hybrids. Coils give firmer support under the heavy middle of the body while the foam on top handles the pressure points. The two cheapest beds are all-foam, which is typical, since foam costs less to make.

blocks.h3: What the table cannot tell you

blocks.p: Firmness labels are not standardized. Nectar rates the Classic 6.5 out of 10, while one Amazon listing calls the same bed firm. Treat every label as a starting point and use the trial to confirm the feel.
Height matters less than the top layers. Look at what the top 3 to 4 inches are made of, not the total thickness.

sections.h: Why Do Side Sleepers Need Pressure Relief at the Shoulder and Hip?

blocks.p: On your side, the shoulder and hip stick out furthest and carry most of your weight. On a firm surface, that concentrated pressure causes the numb arm, the aching hip and the urge to roll over every hour.

A good side sleeper mattress lets the shoulder and hip sink until the waist meets the surface. Then the spine runs roughly straight from neck to tailbone. If the shoulder cannot sink, the upper spine bends. If the hips sink too far, the lower spine sags.

That is why comfort layer thickness matters most for side sleepers. The Helix, Purple and Brooklyn picks each put several inches of soft or adaptive material over their coils, according to their makers and reviewers.

Helix says the Midnight Luxe uses firmer coils under the lower back and softer coils under the shoulders. Owners of non-zoned beds commonly report the trade-off this solves: soft enough for the shoulder lets the hips dip, and firm enough for the hips is hard on the shoulder.

blocks.p: Under about 130 pounds, most medium beds feel firmer than advertised because you do not press far into the comfort layer. Choose soft or medium-soft, or add a topper. RTINGS notes lighter sleepers may not sink far enough into the Brooklyn Signature.
Between roughly 130 and 230 pounds, a medium feel suits most side sleepers. It is the group the Helix Midnight Luxe is designed around.

Above about 230 pounds, soft all-foam beds tend to bottom out at the hips. A hybrid with a sturdy coil core is safer. Our guide to the best mattress for heavy people covers coil gauge, foam density and edge support.

sections.h: Foam or Hybrid: Which Is Better for Side Sleepers?

blocks.p: Both work. Each fits a different kind of side sleeper, and the deciding factors are body weight, heat and how much you move.

Memory foam softens with body heat and slowly molds around the shoulder and hip. The TEMPUR-Cloud and Nectar Classic lean on this feel. The downside is a stuck-in feeling, and reviewers note it makes changing position harder.
All-foam beds also tend to sleep warmer, because dense foam traps heat. Gel and cooling covers help, with mixed results in owner feedback.

A hybrid puts foam over pocketed coils. The coils give firmer support under the hips, add bounce and let air move, which is why hybrids suit heavier and hotter side sleepers. They cost more. Under about 230 pounds, if you sleep cool and like the hug, a foam bed is a sound way to save money.

sections.h: What Is the Best Mattress for Side Sleepers With Hip Pain?

blocks.p: The sore hip is often the one you lie on. A mattress cannot treat the cause, but it can reduce how hard the surface pushes back on the joint. That usually means more cushioning at the hip, with enough support to keep the pelvis level.

Choose a soft or medium feel with a thick comfort layer. The Purple Restore Soft and Helix Midnight Luxe both fit. Purple says its grid collapses under pressure points, and owners commonly describe the hip feeling cradled rather than squeezed.

A bed that is too firm is the classic mistake. For a side sleeper, firm concentrates pressure on the bony point of the hip. If your current bed is firm but sound, a soft topper is a cheaper first experiment.

A pillow between the knees stops the top leg twisting the pelvis. No mattress cures hip pain, though. Hip pain that persists for weeks, wakes you up, or comes with stiffness or swelling warrants a doctor or physical therapist.

sections.h: What Helps Side Sleepers With Shoulder Pain or Back Pain?

blocks.p: A sore shoulder wants a softer top layer. A sore back wants even support under the waist. The best mattress for side sleepers with back pain does both, which is why zoned hybrids keep coming up.

The top 2 to 4 inches do most of the work. Owners commonly report waking with a numb arm on beds that are too firm, a sign the shoulder is not sinking. Pillow height matters too: too low loads the shoulder, too high bends the neck. Lasting shoulder pain, especially with weakness, should be checked by a doctor or physical therapist.

Look for a medium feel with zoned or firmer lumbar support, like the Helix Midnight Luxe. The Leesa and Nectar are slightly firmer options that keep the waist from sagging. Our guide to the best mattress for back pain covers sciatica and firmness in more depth.
Persistent back pain, pain down a leg, or numbness are reasons to see a doctor or physical therapist rather than buy a new bed.

sections.h: What Should Combination Sleepers Look For?

blocks.p: Most side sleepers spend part of the night on their back, and some roll onto their stomach. The mattress has to work in each position and let you move between them easily.
Combination sleepers do better on a responsive surface that springs back quickly. Hybrids are responsive; traditional memory foam is slow, which frustrates anyone who turns over often.
The Leesa Original Hybrid is the pick here, with thinner foam than the Helix and bouncy pocketed coils. Brooklyn Bedding recommends the medium Signature Hybrid for combination sleepers.
For a side and back mix, medium is safest. If you also sleep on your stomach, lean firmer, because a soft bed lets the hips sink and arches the lower back in that position.

sections.h: Can a Pillow or Topper Fix a Mattress That Is Too Firm?

blocks.p: Often, partly. A topper can add the cushioning your shoulder and hip miss on a firm bed in good shape. Nothing on top fixes a mattress that sags or has a body impression.

A 2- to 3-inch memory foam or latex topper is the usual choice for side sleepers. Memory foam hugs deeper; latex is more responsive and cooler. Our guide to the [best mattress toppers](/best-mattress-topper/) compares options for side sleepers and back pain.

Side sleepers need the highest pillow of any position to fill the gap between ear and shoulder. A softer mattress lets the shoulder sink and reduces the loft you need, so pick the mattress first and the pillow second.
A knee pillow keeps the hips stacked. For older side sleepers who want easier entry and exit, our guide to the [best mattress for seniors](/best-mattress-for-seniors/) covers edge support and height.

mistakes: Buying the Firm Mattress Because It Feels Healthier

Firm beds are often sold as better for your body, but for side sleepers a firm surface concentrates pressure on the shoulder and hip. Unless you weigh well over 230 pounds or also sleep on your stomach, a medium or softer feel almost always serves a side sleeper better.

Firmness labels assume an average sleeper. A 120-pound person feels a medium bed as firm, and a 260-pound person feels it as soft. Read every firmness rating through the lens of your own weight, and use the table above to adjust up or down before you choose.
Judging a Mattress in the First Week

Your body needs time to adjust to a new surface, and foam softens as it breaks in. Many makers require 21 to 30 nights before a return for exactly this reason. Give a new bed about a month before deciding, unless it is causing real pain.

A softer mattress lets the shoulder sink, which changes how much pillow loft you need. A pillow that suited a firm bed may now push the head up at an angle. If your neck feels worse after switching mattresses, try a lower or adjustable pillow before blaming the bed.
Using a Topper to Fix a Sagging Bed

A topper adds cushioning, but it cannot restore support. If your current mattress has a dip or a body impression, a topper simply follows the sag, and the hips still drop. Toppers make sense for a firm bed in good shape, not for a worn-out one.
bottomLine: Side sleeping comes down to one balance: enough give at the shoulder and hip, enough support at the waist. For most people that means a medium hybrid like the Helix Midnight Luxe. Lighter sleepers can go softer, heavier sleepers should go sturdier, and anyone who moves around a lot should favor a responsive hybrid over slow memory foam. Whatever you buy, use the trial. Give your body about a month to adjust, swap your pillow if your neck complains, and remember that a mattress makes sleep more comfortable but does not treat pain. If shoulder, hip or back pain persists, a doctor or physical therapist is the right next step, not another mattress.

faqs.q: What is the best mattress for side sleepers?
faqs.a: For most side sleepers, a medium hybrid with a thick comfort layer and zoned support works best. Our top pick is the Helix Midnight Luxe, which Helix designed around side sleepers. Lighter side sleepers may prefer something softer, such as the Purple Restore Soft, while heavier side sleepers should look at a sturdier hybrid like the Brooklyn Signature.

faqs.q: Should side sleepers get a soft or firm mattress?
faqs.a: Most side sleepers do best on a soft to medium mattress, not a firm one. The shoulder and hip need to sink in so the spine stays straight. Body weight shifts the answer: under about 130 pounds, go soft to medium-soft; between 130 and 230, medium; above 230, medium to medium-firm with coil support.

faqs.q: What is the best mattress for side sleepers with hip pain?
faqs.a: Look for a soft or medium mattress with a thick, pressure-relieving top layer and enough support underneath to keep the pelvis level. The Purple Restore Soft and Helix Midnight Luxe both fit. A pillow between the knees also helps keep the hips stacked. Persistent hip pain should be checked by a doctor or physical therapist.

faqs.q: What is the best mattress for side sleepers with back pain?
faqs.a: A medium mattress with zoned or firmer lumbar support suits side sleepers with back pain, because it cushions the shoulder while keeping the waist from sagging. The Helix Midnight Luxe uses firmer coils under the lower back. If pain is persistent, runs down a leg or comes with numbness, see a doctor or physical therapist.

faqs.q: Is memory foam or hybrid better for side sleepers?
faqs.a: Both work. Memory foam gives the deepest contouring and suits lighter side sleepers who like a hugging feel and do not move much. Hybrids add coil support and bounce, so they suit heavier side sleepers, combination sleepers and hot sleepers better. Hybrids generally cost more, which is why most budget picks are foam.

faqs.q: Why does my shoulder hurt when I sleep on my side?
faqs.a: Often the mattress is too firm, so the shoulder cannot sink and takes too much of your weight. A pillow that is too low can add to the strain. A softer mattress or topper and a higher pillow may help. Shoulder pain that lasts, or comes with weakness, should be assessed by a doctor or physical therapist.

faqs.q: Can a mattress topper make a firm mattress better for side sleeping?
faqs.a: Yes, if the mattress is otherwise in good shape. A 2- to 3-inch memory foam or latex topper adds the cushioning a side sleeper's shoulder and hip need, at a fraction of the cost of a new bed. A topper will not fix a mattress that sags or has a body impression, though.
